newsitem.title: GERMANY: West German industry investment to fall in '97 - Ifo.
newsitem.headline: West German industry investment to fall in '97 - Ifo.

text.p: Industrial investment in west Germany, the traditional motor of economic recovery, will fall in real terms in 1997 after growth slows this year, a survey published by the Ifo institute on Thursday showed.
Ifo's survey of 2,000 companies in September and October found that investment would be unchanged in 1997, unadjusted for inflation. But, in real terms, investment will fall by one percent.
Companies have cut back on earlier plans to expand investment this year, with the final investment total forecast at 77 billion marks, up from 75 billion last year.
That puts 1996 investment higher by a nominal five percent, but still a percentage point below Ifo's spring forecast. Investment growth was seven percent in 1995.

Weak industrial investment has rung alarm bells among economists following Germany's unemployment-dogged economy. They say that modest recovery is now being carried by exports, but industry investment must pick up if growth targets of 2.5 percent next year are to be met.
On the positive side, Ifo said investment in raw materials and capital goods is set to rise in 1997 -- but most investment will continue to be in replacing existing equipment.
But rationalisation measures will continue to consume around a quarter of investment outlays, the survey said.
